target_customer: Biotech and pharma companies and research labs that need reagents, or US drug developers needing contract manufacturing without relying on Chinese CDMOs
problem: Labs overpay for reagents and drug developers lack fast US-based manufacturing capacity; Bramante sells lab reagents and media and pitches shipping-container microfactories for contract drug manufacturing.
business_model: Reagent catalog sales (made to order, per unit) plus planned CDMO services
product_category: Life sciences reagents and contract biomanufacturing (CDMO)

founders.name: Scott Stankey
previous_startups: Protein Evolution (industrial biotech turning plastic waste into textile fibers; outcome not found)

founders.name: Mike (surname not on YC page)
education: University of Pennsylvania, PhD Bioengineering (after Penn M&T program as undergraduate)
founders.background_notes: Aggregators name him Michael Magaraci; not confirmed on YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Containerized cGMP biomanufacturing requires regulatory-grade quality systems and process engineering; reagent resale itself is simple, so the hard part is the CDMO plan.

defensibility.rationale: Reagents are commodity products with price competition; a licensed manufacturing footprint could become a regulatory moat but none was evidenced.

incumbents: Established CDMOs such as WuXi Biologics
takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent response recorded for Bramante.

market_need_then: Many US drug developers contract with Chinese manufacturers according to the YC launch page; trade press describes modular cleanrooms as a growing alternative to building facilities.

identity.logo: Beaver logo (bramante-beaver.png on the reagent site)
identity.mascot_or_character: Beaver, used in a 'Busy beaver alert' same-day shipping banner
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and value-focused: 'Fair.', 'More science. Less overhead.', 'Reagents for the lab. Built for discovery. Priced for reality.'

brand_strength.rationale: Clear plain voice and a mascot on the site, but no external coverage and two different offerings under the name.

outcome_analysis: Bramante is a two person Spring 2025 YC company from founders who previously built Protein Evolution. It sells reagents through its site while its YC launch pitches shipping-container drug manufacturing, and no source dates a shift between them. No verified funding, customers or exit were found, so the outcome and any success or failure factors cannot be judged.
notes: Funding unverified: VCBacked lists 500K dollars (pre-seed, June 2025, YC), Dealroom lists 125K seed undated; aggregator only, no round recorded. Competitor search returned only generic 2025 to 2026 modular cleanroom trade pieces, not dated competitors for this company, so the list is empty. Batch shown as P25 or W25 or X25 across aggregators; YC page says Spring 2025. YC page lists offerings as reagents while the YC launch page says CDMO, order and timing unknown. No acquisition, shutdown or layoff news found. Completeness pass: the 500K pre-seed dated 2025-06 rests on a single database (VCBacked); Dealroom lists a 125K seed, so the amount conflicts. The second founder name Michael Magaraci comes from Dealroom and Startupintros, not the YC page, and was not applied.
